instruction:
A debugger maintainer needs a byte-accurate decoder for suspended FreeRTOS RISC-V tasks. Use the earliest stable FreeRTOS-Kernel release whose official release notes announce both floating-point and vector context-save support for the GCC RISC-V port. Use that release's unmodified sources, not the current development branch.

Analyze the interrupted-task save path, not the initial artificial stack for a never-run task. The build uses the bundled chip-specific header for a core with no MTIME, no SiFive CLINT, and no extra chip-specific saved registers. configENABLE_FPU and configENABLE_VPU are both 1; __riscv_fdiv and __riscv_vector are defined; __riscv_32e is absent. VLEN is 128 bits. Analyze all four (__riscv_xlen, __riscv_flen) pairs (32,32), (32,64), (64,32), and (64,64), each with entry FS=Dirty and entry VS either Clean or Dirty. Configuration labels RV32F32, RV32F64, RV64F32 and RV64F64 mean these width pairs; they are labels, not complete ISA strings.

This is a static analysis of the emitted save operations. Assume the stated configurations are preprocessed as given and memory writes complete, including any misaligned writes; do not substitute an ABI's intended layout or repair the code. No nesting or application handler runs during the analyzed save. Let S be task sp on entry, and P be the task sp value saved into the first TCB member. Inspect the completed asynchronous-interrupt context immediately after the saved mepc has been written and before switching to the ISR stack. All offsets below are byte offsets relative to P.

For every configuration/state pair, return the stack-pointer decrement S-P; the beginning of the slot where the entry x1/ra was stored; the beginning of f0; the half-open byte interval written by the fcsr save; the beginning of v0, or NONE if v0 is not saved; and any byte intervals of earlier saved INTEGER REGISTER images overwritten by later save operations. The ra slot location is requested even if some of its bytes are later overwritten. Do not count mstatus, mepc, padding or critical-nesting metadata as integer-register images. For an overwrite, name the affected architectural integer register and the overlapping interval relative to P (not the entire later store). If no such overwrite occurs, write NONE.

Return only a table, sorted by configuration in the order given above and then Clean, Dirty:
configuration | VS | frame_bytes | ra_offset | f0_offset | fcsr_range | v0_offset | overwritten_integer_bytes
Use decimal integers, half-open intervals [start,end), and register:interval pairs separated by semicolons for multiple overwrites. Use NONE only for an absent vector save or absence of integer-image overwrites. Do not treat missing data as NONE.

Suggested method: identify the release and the applicable chip header, follow the interrupt save macros, and keep a running stack pointer. Distinguish register storage widths from the sizes used to reserve stack space. Record writes in order before checking for overlap.
output_format: configuration | VS | frame_bytes | ra_offset | f0_offset | fcsr_range | v0_offset | overwritten_integer_bytes
